rows: Dimension table listing the business areas that corporate spend is attributed to. Joined to the Calculations fact table on Business Area ID.
Dimension describing what money was spent on, organized as a Cost Element Group -> Cost Element Sub Group -> Cost element name hierarchy. Joined to the Calculations fact table on Cost Element ID.
Geography dimension providing the country/region for each spend record and the sales region it rolls up to. Joined to the Calculations fact table on Country/Region ID.
Standard date dimension marked as the model's date table so time-intelligence functions (YTD, prior period, etc.) work. Contains one row per day with calendar attributes (Year, Period, Month).
Dimension listing departments and the VP that owns each one. Joined to the Calculations fact table on Department.

Fact table containing the corporate spend records. Each row is one scenario/day/dimension combination, with Value holding the raw amount. This table also hosts every reporting measure (Actual, Plan, LE1-3, variances, KPI helpers) and when only measure a visible it converts to a measure group and shows at the top of the Data pane so users can find it easily.
Dimension categorizing spend by IT Area and IT Sub Area (IT Area rolls up several IT Sub Areas). Joined to the Calculations fact table on IT Sub Area ID.

Dimension for the planning scenarios that slice the fact table: Actual, Plan, and three Latest Estimates (LE1, LE2, LE3) - the in-year re-forecasts. Every scenario-specific measure filters this table.

Field parameter. Lets a report user switch a visual between showing variance to plan as an absolute dollar amount ([Var to Plan]) or as a percentage ([Var to Plan %]). Drop the '# / %' column onto a slicer and use it as the value on a chart to swap the metric without duplicating visuals.

Field parameter. Lets a report user pick which dimension to break a visual down by - Business Area, Country/Region, Sales Region, IT Area, or IT Sub Area. Put the 'Breakdown by' column on a chart axis and expose it as a slicer so one visual can pivot across many dimensions.
Name of the business area (e.g. Finance, Sales). Used for slicing and grouping in visuals.
Surrogate key that joins Business Area to the Calculations fact table.
Lowest level of the cost taxonomy - the individual line item shown in reports.
Top level of the cost hierarchy (e.g. Hardware, Software, Services).
Middle level of the cost hierarchy; rolls up into Cost Element Group and is made up of Cost element name items.
Surrogate key that joins Cost Element to the Calculations fact table.
Broader sales region a country belongs to (e.g. EMEA, APAC). Use for regional roll-ups.
Raw country/region name as it arrives from the source spreadsheet. Kept for lineage; use 'Country / Region' for reporting because it is cleaned up.
Surrogate key that joins Country Region to the Calculations fact table.
Cleaned-up display country column (fixes the 'New Zeland' typo and trims whitespace). Tagged as data category Country so it works with map visuals.
Calendar date. Grain of the Date table (one row per day).
Fiscal/calendar period number (1-12) used to sort the Month column into calendar order.
Three-letter month name (Jan, Feb, ...). Sorted by Period so visuals show months in calendar order rather than alphabetically.
Name of the VP that owns the department.
Department identifier / name. Joined to the Calculations fact table on Department.
Date the spend was booked on. Hidden - use the Date dimension in reports so time intelligence works.
Raw spend amount for the row. Hidden - report through the [Actual], [Plan], [LE1-3] measures which apply the YTD and scenario logic.
Foreign key to the Department dimension.
Foreign key to the Cost Element dimension.
Foreign key to the Country Region dimension.
Foreign key to the Business Area dimension.
Foreign key to the IT Area dimension (joined at the sub-area grain).
Foreign key to the Scenario dimension; distinguishes Actual vs. Plan vs. Latest Estimate rows.
Top level of the IT taxonomy (e.g. Infrastructure, Applications). Rolls up several IT Sub Areas.
Detailed IT category that rolls up into IT Area (e.g. Networking, ERP).
Surrogate key that joins IT Area to the Calculations fact table.
Short scenario code shown in visuals (e.g. Act, Plan, LE1).
Surrogate key that joins Scenario to the Calculations fact table.
Full scenario name (e.g. Actual, Plan, Latest Estimate 1). This is the column the scenario measures filter on inside CALCULATE.
The choice shown to users: '#' selects the dollar-value variance measure, '%' selects the percentage variance measure.
Hidden. Holds the NAMEOF() references to [Var to Plan] and [Var to Plan %] - Power BI substitutes the chosen measure at query time.
Hidden. Sort order used to keep '#' before '%' in the slicer.
The choice shown to users - Business Area, Country / Region, Sales Region, IT Area, or IT Sub Area - controlling which dimension a visual is broken down by.
Hidden. Holds the NAMEOF() references to each candidate dimension column - Power BI substitutes the chosen column at query time.
Hidden. Sort order that keeps the dimensions in the intended sequence in the slicer.
Year-to-date sum of the raw fact Value, scaled by 0.3 for this demo dataset. This is the base building block that every scenario measure (Actual, Plan, LE1-3) wraps with a CALCULATE filter.
YTD spend for the Actual scenario. Equivalent to [Amount] filtered to ScenarioDescription = 'Actual'.
YTD spend for Latest Estimate 1 (LE1) - the first in-year re-forecast. Equivalent to [Amount] filtered to ScenarioDescription = 'Latest Estimate 1'.
YTD spend for Latest Estimate 2 (LE2) - the second in-year re-forecast. Equivalent to [Amount] filtered to ScenarioDescription = 'Latest Estimate 2'.
YTD spend for Latest Estimate 3 (LE3) - the third in-year re-forecast. Equivalent to [Amount] filtered to ScenarioDescription = 'Latest Estimate 3'.
YTD spend for the original Plan (budget) - [Amount] filtered to ScenarioDescription = 'Plan'.
Dollar variance of Actual vs. the first Latest Estimate (LE1) forecast: [Actual] - [LE1]. Positive means Actual came in above the LE1 forecast.
Dollar variance of Actual vs. the second Latest Estimate (LE2) forecast: [Actual] - [LE2]. Positive means Actual came in above the LE2 forecast.
Dollar variance of Actual vs. the third Latest Estimate (LE3) forecast: [Actual] - [LE3]. Positive means Actual came in above the LE3 forecast.
Dollar variance of Actual vs. Plan: [Actual] - [Plan]. Positive = overspent vs. budget, negative = under budget.
Percentage variance of Actual vs. the first Latest Estimate (LE1) forecast: [Var to LE1] / [LE1]. Safely returns blank when LE1 is 0.
Percentage variance of Actual vs. the second Latest Estimate (LE2) forecast: [Var to LE2] / [LE2]. Safely returns blank when LE2 is 0.
Percentage variance of Actual vs. the third Latest Estimate (LE3) forecast: [Var to LE3] / [LE3]. Safely returns blank when LE3 is 0.
Percentage variance of Actual vs. Plan: [Var to Plan] / [Plan]. This is the value the '# / %' field parameter picks when the user chooses '%'.

KPI measure. Value is [Actual]; target is [Plan]. Status turns green when Actual/Plan < 1 (under budget), yellow up to 1.1 (up to 10% over), red above 1.1 - shown via the 'Traffic Light - Single' KPI graphic.
Returns [Actual] only when the current context is over plan (Var to Plan % > 0); otherwise blank. Used to color/highlight the overspent portion of a chart or KPI.

Returns [Actual] only when the current context is at or under plan (Var to Plan % <= 0); otherwise blank. Pair with [Actual overspent] to color a chart green/red by budget status. (Name kept as spelled in source model.)
Dynamic text for a card/title. Reads 'Overall, we are within our planned spending by $X' when [Var to Plan] <= 0, otherwise 'Overall, we have overspent by $X'.

IF([Var to Plan %]<=0, 
"Overall, we are within our planned spending by ",
"Overall, we have overspent by ")
& format([Var to Plan], "$#,##0")

Label helper for drilling into the IT hierarchy. Returns 'AreaName (Area) SubAreaName (Sub Area)' when both levels are in scope, or just the level that is in scope. Handy as a title or tooltip when a visual can be at either level.

SWITCH ( TRUE(),
    ISINSCOPE('IT Area'[IT Area]) && ISINSCOPE('IT Area'[IT Sub Area]),
        SELECTEDVALUE('IT Area'[IT Area]) & " (Area) " & SELECTEDVALUE('IT Area'[IT Sub Area]) & " (Sub Area)",
    ISINSCOPE('IT Area'[IT Area]), SELECTEDVALUE('IT Area'[IT Area]),
    ISINSCOPE('IT Area'[IT Sub Area]), SELECTEDVALUE('IT Area'[IT Sub Area]),
    BLANK()
)
